first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both deteriorating, making simplification the most directly aligned and likely sustainable intervention. Verify memory_86 because it is central to the proposed action and current metrics have reversed. Verify memory_73 because competitor pricing creates a consequential alternative, but its support for sustainable qualified revenue rather than short-term acquisition remains uncertain. Run a measured onboarding experiment and monitor qualified revenue, not just completion or activation.

mid.rationale: Run a standard, measured test of shortened onboarding because the verified evidence directly addresses both current problems: onboarding completion is down 4% and activation is down 6%, while the prior test improved completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention. Do not pursue promotional pricing: although it lifted qualified revenue 18% initially, 30-day retention fell 12%, creating unacceptable sustainable-revenue risk. Evaluate the onboarding variant on qualified activation, time-to-value, 30-day retention, and downstream qualified revenue—not completion alone.

final2.rationale: Keep the committed onboarding experiment rather than switching to promotional pricing in response to the competitor’s deeper cut. The verified pricing test produced short-term qualified-revenue lift but materially worse 30-day retention, so broad discounting risks unsustainable revenue and should not be generalized without new evidence. Shortened onboarding is verified to improve completion, time-to-value, and retention, directly addressing the current activation and onboarding declines. Monitor price-sensitive SMB churn and segment results separately; do not claim that onboarding alone resolves the competitive pricing threat.
